title: Timex Group: A Name From Time and Kleenex to Versace Watches and Baupost

reader_summary.source_label: From the episode notes — transcript not yet available
reader_summary.headline: In 1941 Norwegian businessman Thomas Olsen bought the Waterbury Clock Company and named its watches Timex.
reader_summary.overview: In 1941 Norwegian businessman Thomas Olsen bought the Waterbury Clock Company and named its watches Timex, a blend of Time magazine and Kleenex. Kleenex then stood for everyday convenience found in nearly every home, and Olsen wanted a watch to be just as common. Today the business is Timex Group BV, an American Dutch holding company based in Middlebury, Connecticut and Hoofddorp in the Netherlands.

key_points.text: Kleenex then stood for everyday convenience found in nearly every home, and Olsen wanted a watch to be just as common.
Today the business is Timex Group BV, an American Dutch holding company based in Middlebury, Connecticut and Hoofddorp in the Netherlands.
Timex Group USA runs Timex and Nautica, Sequel AG handles Guess and GC, Vertime SA makes Versace and Versus watches.
